title: Yijing Hears the Morning Bell
subtitle: Discipline at Dawn in Nalanda’s City of Learning
region: Nalanda's monasteries, pools and lecture halls
moral: Discipline turns a crowd into a community.

sources.citation: Yijing, Da Tang Xiyu Qiu Fa Gaoseng Zhuan, c. 691 CE; trans. J. Takakusu (1896)
sources.note: Primary source for daily monastic practice and rules.

sources.citation: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji, physical description of Nalanda
sources.note: Primary account for buildings, teachers and curriculum.

sources.citation: Frederick Asher, Nalanda (2015); Scharfe, Education in Ancient India (2002)
sources.note: Modern assessment of institutional scale and routines.

panels.shot: wide aerial view of Nalanda at daybreak

dialogue.text: In Nalanda of the seventh century, as dawn bells stirred thousands of monks, Yijing watched and asked: how can a vast city of seekers live by one shared discipline?

panels.shot: slow push-in from darkness to Yijing’s contemplative face

dialogue.text: From far Tang China, Yijing had sailed and ridden for years to reach Nalanda. Now, before sunrise, he hears a soft bell. It is the pulse of this disciplined world.

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Yijing looking into the corridor

dialogue.text: He had read of Vinaya rules in texts. Here he sees them as footsteps in a corridor, as the bell draws every monk, young and old, into one shared rhythm.
In his record, Yijing would note: at dawn, the monks rise, dress properly, and move in order. Nalanda is not a crowd; it is a community shaped by rule.

panels.shot: wide shot of bathing pools, side-on

dialogue.text: Later he writes: before study, the monks bathe in appointed pools. Cleanliness is not a luxury here. It is the first discipline of the day.

panels.shot: closer shot of the pool, focus on rules in action

dialogue.speaker: yijing
dialogue.text: Every gesture is guided. Thousands can bathe without chaos.

panels.shot: medium shot inside a simple refectory hall

dialogue.text: Yijing’s account tells of dining rules: monks sit in order, wait together, and eat only after a sign. Food becomes part of training, not private habit.

panels.shot: close-up on Yijing recording on a palm-leaf manuscript

dialogue.text: His stylus moves and the dawn becomes ink. He sets down: robes of prescribed colours, rules for washing, for sitting, for walking. Nalanda’s order is made visible in words.

panels.shot: wide shot of lecture hall filled with monks

dialogue.text: Xuanzang had praised Nalanda’s halls of debate. Yijing now records the daily discipline that fills those halls: only those who keep the rules may sit and study here.

panels.shot: medium shot of a senior Indian monk speaking with Yijing

dialogue.text: He learns of the Nalanda Nikaya, a body of discipline that governs life here. This is not the rule of one man, but of an agreed code handed down and applied.

panels.shot: close-up on Yijing’s thoughtful face, side-lit

dialogue.text: In his travelogue, he carefully compares Indian practice with Chinese customs. Some habits differ, but the heart is the same: shared rules that allow many to live and learn together.

panels.shot: wide shot showing diversity of monks in the courtyard

dialogue.text: Yijing notes that monks here come from many lands. Nalanda’s discipline binds strangers into fellow students. Without it, distance and number would pull them apart.

panels.shot: medium shot of Yijing offering guidance to a younger foreign monk

dialogue.speaker: yijing
dialogue.text: Follow their rules closely. Then the teachings will open to you.

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Yijing writing in a quiet chamber

dialogue.text: Years later, his work would carry Nalanda’s daily rules back to East Asia. The bells he hears at dawn in Bihar will echo in monasteries across the seas.

panels.shot: evening wide shot of Nalanda courtyard from high angle

dialogue.text: Modern scholars use Yijing’s careful notes to glimpse Nalanda as a working institution: a residential city whose strength lay not only in ideas, but in the rules that carried them.

panels.shot: close-up on Yijing looking up toward the bell tower in twilight

dialogue.text: For Yijing, the morning bell at Nalanda is more than a sound. It is the sign that discipline can turn thousands of separate lives into one shared path of learning.
